notes.made: Rick Roberts, formerly of the Flying Burrito Brothers, wrote it. He had the chorus for months and couldn't make the verses work until he decided he was overthinking it, then finished them in a day or two. Jim Mason produced the album at Criteria in Miami, with Karl Richardson engineering. The flute is David Muse, and the band liked his part so much they made him a full member.
notes.context: Firefall formed in Boulder, Colorado, in 1974, with Byrds drummer Michael Clarke and Mark Andes of Spirit among the founders. Atlantic put the song out as the second single after 'Livin' Ain't Livin'' just missed the top 40. It broke in Chicago and Houston in October 1976 and peaked at 9 in November, and the album went Platinum. Jock Bartley later said it made the band 'a singing version of the Hallmark card', a mixed blessing for a group who thought of themselves as a 'pretty smokin' Rock band'.

listen_for.note: David Muse, the finishing touch that got him into the band. The panel's Purist calls it pure 1976.
The part Roberts wrote first and sat on for months. The verses around it are deliberately plain.

notes.unverified: Wikipedia gives the album two release dates (8 April 1976 on the album page, August 1976 on the song page); both are 1976. The song page credits vocals to Chuck Kirkpatrick without saying lead or backing, so I didn't name a lead singer.

culture.title: Number 9
culture.line: Broke in Chicago and Houston in October 1976 and peaked at 9 that November, with 6 on Easy Listening.

culture.title: Atlantic's fastest gold
culture.line: The 1976 debut album reached 28 and went Platinum, and Wikipedia says it was the fastest record in Atlantic's history to go gold.
